Hi Karthik,

We’re evaluating Redwood for hosted API for a number of production features and procurement is asking for a few clarifications before we move forward:

- Can you share a baseline rate card for hosted API (per-token and embeddings) we can use for internal budgeting?
- Do you support monthly invoicing versus charging a credit card? If so, what are the typical eligibility criteria (committed spend, credit check, or legal/PO in place)?
- What net terms do you offer (Net30/Net45)? Any differences for EU customers (VAT handling) or SEPA support?
- Do you require an MSA for invoicing or will a signed SOW + PO suffice for net terms?

We have a procurement window targeting the end of July and they prefer sample invoice schedules to be able to approve the PO. Could you send the rate card and an example invoice cadence?

Hi Lara,

Thanks for the clear list  happy to help. Quick answers up front, and I’ve attached the rate card + a sample invoice schedule for your procurement team to review.

1) Rate card: attached "Redwood_ratecard_Q3_2025.xlsx". It shows default hosted-API list pricing (generation/embedding units) and our standard volume bands.

2) Billing cadence: by default we use card:auto-charge for self-serve signups. For enterprise customers we offer monthly invoicing on approved credit (typically Net30). Eligibility usually requires either: an annual/6-month committed spend, or a credit application + PO + signed MSA. We can be flexible for pilot programs.

3) Net terms: Net30 is standard for invoiced accounts; Net45 is possible with underwriting approval. For EU customers we can show VAT on invoices and accept SEPA on a case-by-case basis (we usually prefer ACH/ACH-equivalent for US accounts).

4) Contracting: a signed MSA speeds enablement for invoicing. If you need us to accept a PO as sufficient, Sales Ops will need to confirm your billing contact and run a brief credit check.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop Sales Ops (Marissa) to get a credit application and set up e-invoicing.
- Marissa/Neha: please prepare the example invoice cadence and a checklist for the procurement team (billing contact, PO number, remit instructions).

Lara, I’ve attached: Redwood_ratecard_Q3_2025.xlsx and example-invoice-schedule.pdf. If you can share an expected monthly spend range, we can also run a quick discount model for committed volumes.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
